clue.text: Damned tired en passant, this should give one a lift

definitions.text: this should give one a lift

indicators.note: damned suggests the words are ruined or wrecked, so the letters of tired en passant are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weary passer-by is told something will cheer them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damned' signals rearranging the fourteen letters of TIRED EN PASSANT. The definition is playful: the 'lift' is to the spirits, not a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a drug is taken to raise a low mood, a figurative lift.

clue.text: Foster being untrue? Possibly about right

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters are placed around the letter for right
possibly hints that the word untrue could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a foster parent is being dishonest, and whether that is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges UNTRUE to NUTURE, and 'about' puts that round R. 'Foster' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster a child or a talent is to raise and encourage it, a synonym.

clue.text: Apt in time to change being restlessly eager

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of apt in time to be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keen for change is fidgety and keen to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges the nine letters of APT IN TIME; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to wait calmly is restless and keen, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Squeeze former partner with wrongful act

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: An ex-partner is pressured into some legal misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is the legal term for a civil wrong, such as negligence or trespass.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze someone for money is to obtain it by pressure or threats, a synonym.

clue.text: Check trainers for repair

indicators.note: something sent for repair is broken and remade, so the letters of trainers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone inspects sports shoes that have been sent to be mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for repair' rearranges TRAINERS; 'Check' is a verb meaning hold back, not inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or curb it, a synonym.

clue.text: Heard views in certain spots

indicators.note: heard means the word for views is spoken and the spelling follows its sound

parts.note: sights are views or things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone has heard about scenic outlooks at particular places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' signals a word that sounds the same: SIGHTS (views) is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are particular locations, places set aside for a purpose.

clue.text: A group broadcasting in desert

parts.note: a band is a musical group
a programme that is broadcasting is on air

explanation.surface: A band plays a radio show out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun for sandy country; here it is the verb meaning leave behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to leave them for good, a synonym.

clue.text: Suffering defeat, charming sailor scoffing

parts.note: taking is an old adjective for charming or attractive
AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
scoffing is informal for eating greedily

explanation.surface: A charming sailor wolfs down food while suffering a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' as an adjective means attractive; AB is an able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roundly beaten in a contest is an idiom for losing heavily.

clue.text: Job with newspaper is where to get good living

definitions.meaning: a position on the staff of the Sun, a British tabloid newspaper
a favourable, comfortable spot in life

explanation.surface: A newspaper post is offered as the route to the good life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British daily tabloid, so a job there is literally a place at it; the phrase also means a position of comfort and prosperity.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a staff post at a tabloid, and an idiom for a favoured, prosperous position.

clue.text: Soldier favoured protection from fire

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a pet student or project is a favoured one

explanation.surface: A favourite soldier finds shelter from gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: PARA is short for paratrooper; the definition is the low wall on a fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A low defensive wall on a rampart shields troops from enemy shots.

clue.text: Hinder what TV rental company sometimes wants

definitions.meaning: to hold up or delay progress

definitions.text: what TV rental company sometimes wants
definitions.meaning: a rental firm wants its television returned when the hire ends

explanation.surface: A firm that rents out televisions sometimes wants them returned.
explanation.walkthrough: TV rental was common in Britain: firms hired out sets and took them back when payments stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to delay progress, and the television returned to its owner.

clue.text: One playing away with mature person has the Queen, twice

parts.note: an adult is a grown-up, mature person

indicators.note: twice asks for the royal abbreviation to be written two times in a row

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A grown-up away from home has an audience with the Queen on two occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina; 'playing away' is British slang for being unfaithful, borrowed from away fixtures in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfaithful to a spouse is said, in slang, to be cheating away from home.

clue.text: Type of chair manufactured by Danes

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters of danes are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A sort of chair is produced by Danish makers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges DANES; the sedan chair was carried on poles by two bearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan was an enclosed seat carried on poles, a kind of portable chair.

clue.text: Opening detective allowed

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A detective gets permission to start an investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: EYE as in 'private eye'; the opening is a small hole for a lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reinforced hole for a lace or cord, a kind of aperture.

clue.text: Where to find Richmond lass?

definitions.meaning: Richmond is the state capital of this US state

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a girl from Richmond might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond is also a London borough and a Yorkshire town, which pulls the solver towards England.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the US state whose capital is Richmond, and a woman's first name.

clue.text: Musical terms that could be represented as sliding

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters of as sliding are reordered

explanation.surface: Terms used in music are said to be portrayed as a sliding effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be represented' rearranges AS SLIDING; the plural is Italian, and the sense nods to the sliding in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: These are directions for a rapid slide through a scale, plural of an Italian music word.

clue.text: Private rights about nothing — it's tosh

parts.note: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is slang for a British private soldier

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for rights goes round the letter for nothing

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon
O, zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A soldier's rights are dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins was the generic name for a British private soldier; 'Private' at the start looks like an adjective about rights. 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is nonsense, and so is this informal word for rubbish.

clue.text: Swimming race includes volunteers

indicators.note: includes means the word for race holds the volunteers abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A swimming race has volunteers taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like part of the swimming picture but means a people, NATION; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the formal or technical word for the act of swimming.

clue.text: Capitol hacks like this newspaper

indicators.note: hacks means cuts up roughly, so the letters of capitol are chopped into a new order

explanation.surface: Journalists covering Congress resemble this paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacks' looks like journalists, but is the verb for chopping, rearranging CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper deals with current affairs, so it is concerned with matters of the moment.

clue.text: In Yorkshire, the outcome is a piece of paper

parts.note: Yorkshire dialect shortens the to t', written as a single T
an issue is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: In Yorkshire the result is merely a scrap of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'up t' mill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, soft paper such as a paper handkerchief is a kind of flimsy sheet.

clue.text: Looking for a helicopter, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the helicopter name is spoken, and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: the Sea King is a well-known military helicopter

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be searching for a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Westland Sea King served with Britain's navy and air-sea rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in search of something is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Very sad newspaper in nervous reaction

indicators.note: in places the paper word inside the twitch word

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitch
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A gloomy newspaper story provokes a twitch.
explanation.walkthrough: RAG is slang for a low-quality newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deeply sorrowful or calamitous is distressing in the extreme.

clue.text: Work during strike or go away

indicators.note: during means the work abbreviation comes within the word for strike

parts.note: to hit is to strike
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: During industrial action, a worker is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; here it means HIT. OP is opus, a work.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a British slang command to leave at once, like 'clear off'.

clue.text: Henry's going into rent projection for plant

indicators.note: going into means the henry symbol is placed inside the word for rent

parts.note: rent, the past of rend, means torn
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Henry is putting the rent towards a forecast for a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like payment but is the past tense of rend, TORN; 'plant' looks industrial but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp pointed outgrowth on a stem, such as on a rose, is a spike sticking out.

clue.text: Complex situation of steersman at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or lost, so the letters of steersman are muddled

explanation.surface: A helmsman out on the ocean finds himself in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' fits the steersman's picture but signals rearranging STEERSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddled, chaotic state of affairs is an idiom built on an imaginary discovery.

clue.text: Help one easily deceived, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for a gullible person is spoken and its sound gives the spelling

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person

explanation.surface: We are told that help went to someone gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: The British pronunciation makes the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal word for aid or relief given in hardship.

clue.text: Violet's partner, gentleman Scotsman

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Violet's companion is a Scottish gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gentian violet is an antiseptic dye, so the plant name pairs with Violet; 'Violet' looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the first half of the dye name gentian violet, so it partners that colour word.

clue.text: They give ladies a run for their money

definitions.text: They give ladies a run for their money

parts.words: They give ladies a run for their money
parts.note: a run is a ladder in hosiery, so these garments may give their buyers a run, not a contest

explanation.surface: Something gives women a tough challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a run for their money' means a stiff contest; here a run is a ladder in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer leg garments for women ladder easily, and a ladder is called a run.
